Rashi on Shabbat 73a:1:1.hebrew: דסבור שומן הוא ואכלו - והיינו דשגג — דסבור שומן הוא, ולא נתכוין לאכול חלב, וחייב. ואף על פי דמתעסק הוא לרבא — דהא לא מתכוין לאכילת איסור — חייב, דאמר שמואל בכריתות (פ"ד דף יט:): בחלבי' ועריות מתעסק חייב, שכן נהנה; אבל בשבת פטור, דלא נהנה. והיינו סייעתא לדידיה, דאמר: נתכוין לחתוך את התלוש וחתך את המחובר — פטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:1:1.english: Where he thought that it was [permitted] fat, and ate it - And this is [what is meant by] "he erred": that he thought it was [permitted] fat and did not intend to eat [forbidden] fat; and [yet] he is liable. And even though according to Rava he is a mit’assek [acting without intent] — since he did not intend [to perform] an eating of a forbidden substance — [nevertheless] he is liable, for Shmuel said in Keritot (chapter 4, daf 19b): Regarding [forbidden] fats and [forbidden] sexual relations, a mit’assek is liable, because he derives pleasure; but on Shabbat he is exempt, because he does not derive pleasure. And this is a support for his [view] (Rava's), who said: [If] one intended to cut detached [produce] and cut attached [produce], he is exempt.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:1:2.hebrew: ואביי - אמר לך: לעולם כי האי גוונא אף בשבת חייב, דלאו מתעסק הוא. והיכי דמי מתעסק דשאר מצות חייב? קסבר רוק הוא — שהיה חלב נימוח — ובלעו, דלא איכוין לאכילה, דרוק לאו בר אכילה הוא אלא בליעה, דכתיב (איוב ז׳:י״ט) "עד בלעי רוקי", ועלתה בידו אכילה, דהא לא איכוין לאכילה. ודכוותייהו דשבת דפטור — נתכוין להגביה, ועלתה בידו חתיכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:1:2.english: And Abaye - [He] could say to you: In truth, in a case like this, [one is] liable even on Shabbat, as he is not [considered] a mit'asek [one acting without intent]. And what are the circumstances of a mit'asek regarding other mitzvot [who is] liable? [Where] he thought it was spittle — for it was melted forbidden fat — and swallowed it, so that he did not intend to eat, as spittle is not an object of eating, but rather of swallowing, as it is written (Job 7:19): "Until I swallow my spittle"; and an act of eating resulted in his hand, for he did not intend to eat. And the counterpart to this on Shabbat, where he is exempt — [is where] he intended to lift [a detached plant], and cutting resulted in his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:2:1.hebrew: דהא לא איכוין לזריקה דאיסור - ויהא שוגג בשבת או במלאכה, אבל זה אינו שוגג לא בשבת ולא במלאכות, אלא מתעסק בדבר אחד של היתר, ועלתה בידו איסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:2:1.english: As he did not intend a prohibited throw - [Such] that he would be [considered] an unwitting transgressor regarding Shabbat or regarding [the] labor; but this [person] is not an unwitting transgressor, neither regarding Shabbat nor regarding [prohibited] labors, but rather [he is] one who acts without intent [mit'asek] regarding a permitted matter, and a prohibited [action] came about through his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:3:1.hebrew: וצריכא - לאיפלוגי בכולהו, אף על גב דדמי להדדי:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:3:1.english: And it is necessary - [For them] to disagree in all of them, even though they are similar to one another:

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:3:2.hebrew: דארבע בלא תרתי לא מזדריק - וזה שנתכוין לשתים וזרק ארבע, נעשית מחשבתו, דהא יש בכלל ד' שתים; הלכך, לאו מתעסק הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:3:2.english: For four [cubits] cannot be thrown without two - And this [person] who intended [to throw] two [cubits] and threw four, his intention was realized, as two are included within four; therefore, he is not [considered] an inadvertent actor [mit'asek].

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:3:3.hebrew: דלא איכוין לזריקה דארבע - ובציר מהני, לא שם זריקה עלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:3:3.english: For he did not intend a throw of four [cubits] - And [for] less than these, the designation of “throwing” does not apply to it.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:3:4.hebrew: אבל כסבור רה"י הוא וכו' - דנתכוין לזריקה גמורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:3:4.english: However, [if one] thought it was a private domain, etc. - For he intended a complete [act of] throwing.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:4:1.hebrew: משכחת לה - להאי שנשתכחה תורת כל הלכות שבת ממנו, ואפילו הכי חשיבא ליה כזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות לחיוביה אכל חדא. כגון דידע ליה לשבת באיסורין, וטעה בשיעורין — שנתכוין לפחות מכשיעור ועשה כשיעור, דלכולן יש שיעור:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:4:1.english: You find that circumstance - For this [person], from whom the concept of all the laws of Shabbat was forgotten, and even so it is considered for him as intentional [regarding] Shabbat and unwitting [regarding] the labors to obligate him for each and every [labor]. For example, where he was aware of Shabbat regarding prohibitions, but erred regarding measures — in that he intended [to perform] less than the [prohibited] measure, but performed the [full] measure, for all of them have a measure.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:4:2.hebrew: אלא לרבא דאמר פטור היכי משכחת לה - דמיחייב שום אדם על כל מלאכה ומלאכה שבהעלם אחד? על כרחך, בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות הוא דבעית לאשכוחיה. והכא דאיעלימו כולהו מיניה, מאי זדון שבת איכא? במה ניכר לו שבת משאר ימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:4:2.english: However, according to Rava, who said [that he is] exempt, how can you find it - That any person would be liable for each and every labor in a single lapse of awareness? Perforce, it is [specifically] in [a case of] intentional [awareness of] Shabbat and unwitting [ignorance of the] labors that you must find it. And here, where all of them were hidden from him, what intentional [awareness of] Shabbat is there? In what way was Shabbat discernible to him from other days?

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:6:1.english: One who winnows - With a winnowing shovel into the wind.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:6:2.english: One who selects - [Removes] refuse with his hands.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:6:3.hebrew: המרקד - בנפה. ובגמ' פריך: הני כולהו חדא היא, דלהפריש פסולת מתוך אוכל נעשות שלשתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:6:3.english: One who sifts - With a sieve. And in the Gemara it challenges: Aren't all of these one [and the same], since all three of them are performed to separate waste from food?

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:6:4.hebrew: האופה - לא הוה במשכן, דלא שייך אלא בפת, ופת לא שייכא במלאכת המשכן. אבל כולהו קמייתא הואי בסממנין של צבע תכלת וארגמן ותולעת שני. ובגמרא פריך: דשביק תנא מבשל דהוי בסממנים, ונקט אופה? ושיעורן של אלו כגרוגרת, חוץ מחורש דבכל שהוא, לקמן בפרק הבונה (שבת דף קג.):
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:6:4.english: One who bakes - [This] was not in the Tabernacle, as it applies only to bread, and bread was not involved in the work of the Tabernacle. However, all the earlier ones were [performed] for the dye ingredients of sky-blue, purple, and scarlet [wool]. And in the Gemara it asks: [Why] did the Tanna omit cooking, which was [performed] with the dye ingredients, and mention baking? And the measure of [liability for] these is the size of a dried fig, except for plowing, which is in any amount, as [stated] below in the chapter [entitled] HaBoneh (Shabbat 103a).

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:1.english: One who shears wool - And all the other labors pertain to wool [used] for the work of the Tabernacle.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:2.english: One who whitens it - [One who] washes it in a river.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:3.english: One who combs it - *Charpir* in Old French [meaning to card wool or unravel fibers].

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:4.english: One who stretches the warp - *Ordir* [in Old French, meaning] to warp [arranging the warp threads before weaving].

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:5.hebrew: בתי נירין - ליצ"ש — שנתן שני חוטין בתוך הבית ניר. ובגוזז ובמלבן וכולהו אינך, מפרש שיעורן לקמן בפרק האורג:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:5.english: Heddle-eyes - *Lices* [heddles] — that one inserted two threads into the heddle-eye. And regarding shearing, whitening, and all the other [labors], [the Mishnah] explains their measures later, in the chapter [entitled] HaOreg.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:6.hebrew: הפוצע - מנתק. פעמים שיש בשני חוטין יותר מדאי, ומנתק מהן ומקלישן לצורך. והני כולהו — ממיסך ואילך עד קושר ומתיר — שייכי ביריעות, ולקמן מפרש מאי קושר ומאי מתיר איכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:6.english: One who severs - Detaching: sometimes there is too much in two threads, and he detaches [strands] from them and thins them for a [constructive] need. And all of these — from "one who warps" onwards until "one who ties" and "one who unties" — pertain to the curtains [of the Tabernacle], and below [the Gemara] explains what [act of] tying and what [act of] untying there were.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:7.english: And one who sews and one who tears - [This] was [performed] on the curtains [of the Tabernacle].

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:8.hebrew: על מנת לתפור - פעמים שהנקב עגול, ואינו יכול לתופרו יפה אא"כ קורעו, כדמפרש בגמרא. אבל קורע שלא לתפור, לא הוי במשכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:7:8.english: In order to sew - Sometimes the hole is round, and one cannot sew it neatly unless one tears it, as the Gemara explains. But tearing not in order to sew did not occur in the Mishkan.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:8:1.english: One who traps a deer - And all the labor [involving] its hide applied to the teḥashim for the Tabernacle, with their hides.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:8:2.english: One who salts it - [This refers] to the hide.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:8:3.english: [One who] smooths it - He scrapes off its hair.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:8:4.english: One who cuts it - [He] trims it and cuts it into straps and sandals.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:9:1.hebrew: כותב ומוחק - לקמן (שבת דף קג:) מפרש למאי מיבעיא למשכן: שכן רושמין על קרשי המשכן לידע איזה בן זוגו, וכותב אות בזו ואות בזו; ומוחק — פעמים שטעה:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:9:1.english: [One who] writes and [one who] erases - Later on (Shabbat 103b), [the Gemara] explains for what [purpose] it was needed in the Mishkan: For they would mark the planks of the Mishkan to know which was its pair, and one would write a letter on this [one] and a letter on that [one]; and erasing — [was needed when] sometimes one erred.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:9:2.english: [One who] extinguishes and [one who] kindles - [These were performed in the Tabernacle] with the fire beneath the cauldron of dyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 73a:9:3.hebrew: מכה בפטיש - הוא גמר כל מלאכה, שכן אומן מכה בקורנס על הסדן להחליקו בגמר מלאכה. ומתניתין נמי לא מיחייב ליה אלא בגמר מלאכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 73a:9:3.english: Striking with a hammer - This is the completion of any craft, for a craftsman strikes with a hammer upon the anvil to smooth it at the completion of work. And our Mishnah, too, holds him liable only for the completion of work.

Tosafot on Shabbat 73a:1:1.hebrew: אלא לאו רישא בע"ז וסיפא בשאר מצות - תימה לר"י: דלוקמא כולה בשאר מצות! ומאי "מה שאין כן בשאר מצות"? כגון שחט וזרק בחוץ, דאינו חייב אלא אחת, כדאמר אביי בפרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין לד:): "שם תעשה" — עשאן הכתוב עשיה אחת. ור' אבהו נמי דפליג, מודה דלרבי ישמעאל בשחיטה וזריקה, ולר' עקיבא בהעלאה וזריקה, דאינו חייב אלא אחת, דמחד קרא נפקי. ושגג בלא מתכוין — כגון שנתכוין לשחוט בהמת חולין והיה צריך לשל חולין, ונמצאת של קדשים; דכוותה בשבת: נתכוין לחתוך תלוש ונמצא מחובר, ולא היה צריך אלא לתלוש, דפטור, דמלאכת מחשבת בעינן. וי"ל: דלא מצינן לפרושי הכי, דמשמע דפטור בשבת לפי ששגג בלא מתכוין, דכה"ג אפילו נתכוין למחובר זה ונמצא מחובר אחר פטור, דאין זה מלאכת מחשבת. וליכא לאוקמי נמי דמיירי כשנעשה מחשבתו, כגון שהיה צריך לחתוך מה שחתך אלא שהיה סבור שהוא תלוש ונמצא שהוא מחובר — הא ליכא למימר, דכה"ג אם פטור לענין שבת מ"אשר חטא בה", פטור נמי לענין חוץ. ומיהו עוד קשה: דלוקמא כולה בשאר מצות, כגון נרבע לזכר ורבע את הזכר, והבא על הבהמה והביא בהמה עליו, דבין לאביי ובין לר' אבהו, לר' עקיבא אינו חייב אלא אחת. והשתא, "שגג בלא מתכוין" מיתוקם שפיר, דמיפטר בשבת מ"אשר חטא בה" — וכגון שנעשית מחשבתו — וגבי עריות לא מיפטר, שכן נהנה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 73a:1:1.english: "Rather, is it not that the first clause is with regard to idolatry and the latter clause with regard to other mitzvot?" - It is puzzling to the Ri: Let [the Gemara] establish the entire [baraita as dealing] with other mitzvot! And what is [the meaning of] "which is not the case with other mitzvot" [in the first clause]? For example, where one slaughtered and sprinkled [the blood of a sacrificial offering] outside [the Temple courtyard], where he is liable for only one [sin-offering], as Abaye said in the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 34b): "'There you shall do' [Deuteronomy 12:14] — the verse rendered them a single act." And Rabbi Abbahu too, who disagrees [with Abaye], concedes that according to Rabbi Yishmael regarding slaughtering and sprinkling, and according to Rabbi Akiva regarding offering up [on an altar] and sprinkling, he is liable for only one, because they are derived from a single verse. And [the case of] "unwitting without intent" [in the latter clause would be], for example, where he intended to slaughter a non-sacred animal and he needed a non-sacred [animal], and it was found to be a consecrated [animal]; and the corresponding case on Shabbat is where he intended to cut a detached [plant] and it was found to be attached [to the ground], and he only needed a detached [plant], where he is exempt, as we require intentional labor [melekhet machashevet]. And it can be answered that we cannot explain [the baraita] this way, because it implies that he is exempt on Shabbat [specifically] because he acted unwittingly without intent, whereas in such a case, even if he had intended for this attached [plant] and it was found to be another attached [plant], he would be exempt, as this is not intentional labor. Nor can one establish [the baraita] as dealing with [a case] where his intention was fulfilled, for example where he needed to cut that which he cut, but he thought it was detached and it was found to be attached — this cannot be said, for in such a case, if he is exempt with regard to Shabbat from [the verse] "wherein he has sinned" [Leviticus 4:23], he is also exempt with regard to [slaughtering] outside. However, it is further difficult: Let [the Gemara] establish the entire [baraita as dealing] with other mitzvot, such as one who was submitted to sodomy with a male and sodomized a male, and one who copulated with an animal and had an animal copulate with him, for both according to Abaye and according to Rabbi Abbahu, according to Rabbi Akiva he is liable for only one! And now, "unwitting without intent" is well established [in the latter clause], for he is exempt on Shabbat from "wherein he has sinned" — and [this is] in a case where his intention was fulfilled — whereas regarding forbidden sexual relations he is not exempt, as he derived pleasure.

Tosafot on Shabbat 73a:7:1.hebrew: העושה שני בתי נירין - צריך לפרש: למה פירש כאן, ובאורג, ובפוצע, ובתופר, ובכותב שיעור, טפי מבשאר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 73a:7:1.english: "One who constructs two meshes" - It is necessary to explain why [the Tanna] specified a measure here, and regarding [one who] weaves, and [one who] severs [threads], and [one who] sews, and [one who] writes, more than for the rest [of the primary labors].

Tosafot on Shabbat 73a:7:2.hebrew: הקושר והמתיר - צ"ע אי מיחייב במתיר שלא על מנת לקשור אי לא. ומדלא תני ליה כדתני מוחק ע"מ לכתוב אין לדקדק, דהכי נמי לא קתני סותר ע"מ לבנות, ובפ' במה מדליקין (לעיל שבת לא:) אמרינן בהדיא דבעינן סותר ע"מ לבנות. ולפי מה שפירש רש"י בגמרא (דף עד:), דאי מתרמי ליה תרי קיטרי בהדי הדדי בשני חוטין זה אצל זה שרי חד ומניח חד — משמע דמיחייב בלא על מנת לקשור; ולשון קטר לא משמע כפירושו. אבל ר"ח פירש, וכן משמע בירושלמי: כשנפסק חוט בשני מקומות ונקשר, מתירין ב' הקשרים ומשליכין לחוץ האמצעי, וחוזרין וקושרין שתי הראשים זה בזה, ואין בו אלא קשר א'; ולפי זה משמע דבעי מתיר ע"מ לקשור. והא דלא תני ליה במתיר ובסותר, פירשתי בפרק ב' (דף לא:) ד"ה וסותר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 73a:7:2.english: One who ties, and one who unties - It requires examination whether one is liable for untying not in order to tie, or not. And from [the fact] that [the Mishnah] does not teach it as it teaches "one who erases in order to write," no inference can be drawn, for it also does not teach "one who demolishes in order to build," and in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (above, Shabbat 31b) we say explicitly that we require demolishing in order to build. And according to what Rashi explained in the Gemara (74b) — that if two knots happened to be adjacent to one another in two threads next to each other, one unties one and leaves one — this implies that one is liable [for untying even] not in order to tie; but the wording "katar" [in the Gemara] does not support his explanation. But Rabbeinu Chananel explained, and so it implies in the Yerushalmi: When a thread tore in two places and was knotted, one unties the two knots and discards the middle [piece], and then ties the two ends to each other, so that there is only one knot in it; and according to this, it implies that one requires untying in order to tie. And that which [the Mishnah] does not teach it regarding untying and demolishing, I explained in Chapter 2 (31b), s.v. Ve-soter.
